findings.shape: A selected mature spreading cedar has a forked lower trunk, layered horizontal axes, evergreen short-shoot needle rosettes, single long-shoot needles and upright barrel-shaped woody seed cones with a subdued apex.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual institutional diagnosis through search retrieval: upright barrel-shaped woody seed cones on short shoots, flat/depressed apex; regional taxonomic boundaries differ among authors and are not resolved by model. Selected actual university arboretum account through search retrieval: evergreen rosette needles on short shoots versus spiral long shoots, four-sided leaves, upright barrel cones disintegrating while an axis remains. No cone disintegration model fitted.
corrections: Added a forked spreading habit, 32 irregular principal branches and three-dimensional secondary short-shoot needle rosettes.
Replaced separated fan-like cone scales with closed original spiral scale-region cues and corrected the selected upright cone to a broader barrel proportion.
Reframed reproductive focus to include actual selected-organ bounds; retained woody axes and individual leaves during sway.
findings.residual: The old-tree crown is still more open and regular than the photographed tree. Fine cone laminae remain smooth and simplified, needle proportions and allometry are unmeasured, and natural bark/needle optics are not calibrated. Cone disintegration and age/population variation are not animated; regional cedar taxonomic boundaries remain source-dependent.
